mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and subsequently drives up the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where GDP growth exceeds 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives down the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to decreased consumer spending and subsequently drive down the S&P 500 over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of instances where the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a growing economy, which can lead to higher demand for goods and services, driving up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where industrial production growth exceeds 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts increase and the federal funds rate is below 4%, it signals a strong demand for housing and a favorable monetary environment, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where housing starts exceed 2000 and the federal funds rate is below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the money supply indicate an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where the federal funds rate is below 4% and the money supply exceeds $350,000.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment and a decrease in the unemployment rate indicate a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and subsequently drive up the S&P 500 over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances where payroll employment exceeds 130,000 and the unemployment rate is below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production and an increase in the consumer price index indicate a decrease in supply and an increase in demand, leading to higher prices and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where industrial production is below 105 and the consumer price index exceeds 195.
